doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

title: Sonny & Cher reunion on the show
summary: He recalls preparing for 'I Got You Babe' with Cher, using his OBX-A oboe and Kurzweil harpsichord.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I watched this morning on YouTube the scene with Sonny & Cher. And I just couldn’t help but put myself in your place because I pictured you — “Oh they might do this song, I’ve got to have an oboe sound for one thing”
And it seemed spontaneous but I suspect that you were sort of prepared for it.

We were prepared for the possibility of it. Cher was pretending that she didn’t want to do it, but you know it was a pretty good possibility. Nonetheless our focus was on her number. She had a rock number, climbing the charts at the time and wanted to play that. She made a rock resurgence right at this time. It may have been [sings] “I have found someone” that song. [sings] “To take away the loneliness.” It could have been that one. So we did that and we had time within about fifty minutes — 5-0 — that we have to get the mix right and stuff. And then after she left the stage I said let’s run through, “I Got You Babe” — very possibly. You know. They’d probably do it. And I just happened to, I have the same two synthesizers, antiques really, for the whole run because I just didn’t have the time to learn something new but I just knew I could get an oboe right out of my OBX-A and a harpsichord down here on the Kurzweil and I’m all set. You know. And so, and everybody kind of knew it too.
Including the modulation which you did very well.
Right from the record you know. You’ve got to do that. But it sure was fun that one, and I guess the last time they ever performed it together.

Yes. And it was interesting, I was happy that near the end the camera panned over where we could see you and most of the band, and I got to watch your conducting style. You know you conduct with your head a lot.
